history.content: Explain how a hash map works in a few sentences.

A hash map stores key-value pairs in an array of buckets. A hash function turns each key into a bucket index, so lookups, inserts and deletes take constant time on average. When two keys land in the same bucket, the map resolves the collision, for example with a linked list or probing.

Is it safe to store passwords with SHA-256?
Not on its own. SHA-256 is fast, which helps attackers who guess billions of passwords per second. Use a slow, salted password hash such as Argon2id, bcrypt or scrypt instead.
